headline: Growth accelerates, losses narrow, gross margin compresses
summary_short: Cloudflare's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 33.5% y/y (+4.1% q/q) to $639.8M, with GAAP net loss narrowing to $22.9M ($0.07/share) from $38.5M a year ago even as gross margin compressed to 71.2% from 75.9%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 33.5% y/y (+4.1% q/q) to $639.8M, driven by more large customers (4,416 vs 3,527 a year ago, each >$100K annualized revenue) and a 118% net retention rate. Gross margin compressed to 71.2% from 75.9% y/y on higher third-party technology, colocation/bandwidth, and depreciation costs. GAAP operating margin improved to -9.7% from -11.1% y/y as revenue outgrew opex growth (S&M +27%, R&D +31%), though the operating loss still widened in dollar terms to $62.0M. Net loss narrowed to $22.9M ($0.07/share) from $38.5M. Cash rose 356% y/y to $932.2M, mainly from the $2.0B convertible notes issued June 2025. The 10-Q discloses no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: MD&A attributes growth to new large-customer wins, expansion within the existing base (118% net retention), and continued international demand (51% of revenue); no single overriding narrative is given beyond these disclosed drivers.
Growth driven by an increase in customers with >$100,000 in annualized revenue (4,416 from 3,527) plus expansion within existing customers, reflected in a 118% dollar-based net retention rate.
Cost of revenue rose on $30.9M more third-party technology services, $15.7M more colocation/bandwidth costs for network expansion, and $11.6M more depreciation from server deployments.
Margin improved y/y because revenue grew 33.5% while opex grew more slowly (S&M +27%, R&D +31%); the operating loss still widened in dollar terms since costs remained ahead of gross profit.
Loss narrowed y/y as revenue growth outpaced the increase in operating costs and interest income rose 88%; the filing does not separately narrate the net-income line.
The y/y increase is mainly from the $2.0 billion 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030, issued in June 2025 with net proceeds of $1,971.0 million, which fell between the two comparison periods.
